messages:
Sasha: quick check — running into a weird combo of ESM/CJS and bundler issues when using the Node/TS SDK in edge runtimes. Next (edge) + Vite apps: sometimes imports fail with "Cannot use import statement outside a module", other times streaming responses drop the Authorization header on reconnects. anyone else seen this?

Lee: yup saw something similar last week in a SvelteKit project. root cause ended up being we were shipping a CJS-only entry in the package `main` and Vite was trying to load it as ESM. the workaround was to use the ESM build for edge bundles.

Maria: fwiw our SDK distribution should expose dual entrypoints. for consumers: in package.json make sure you pick the right import. e.g. in vite/next edge files use:

```js
// dynamic import to force ESM resolution in edge
const { RedwoodClient } = await import('@redwood/inference/esm');
const c = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY });
```

Lee: alternatively add a tiny wrapper that re-exports the ESM entry so `import` works in both dev and prod.

John: streaming + auth issue — reconnects from the runtime (e.g. client-side event stream fallback) were hitting our auth refresh path which returns 302/401 briefly, and the edge platform stripped the header on the retry. two practical fixes: 1) keep a server-side long-lived token for edge functions, 2) on client streams attach a signed URL / one-time token in the query so the reconnect doesn't require a header.

Sasha: can you paste the minimal config that worked for Vite? I'm trying to make the repo reproducible for the docs PR.

Maria: yep. in vite.config.ts I used this plugin shim to prefer the ESM field and avoid commonjs transforms for the SDK package:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
export default defineConfig({
  optimizeDeps: { include: [] },
  ssr: {
    noExternal: ['@redwood/inference']
  }
});
```

That plus importing the `/esm` bundle fixed the import error in their edge build.

Lee: note for Next edge (app dir routes) you also need to ensure the file is under `app/` and runtime is set: `export const runtime = 'edge';` otherwise it will try to use a Node runtime and blow up on ESM-only builds.

Sasha: thanks. what about CI/linting? some of our tests run in Node CJS env and fail on the ESM-only build.

John: we solved that by publishing a CJS compatibility entrypoint (`lib/cjs/index.js`) and pointing `main` to it, while `module` points to ESM. tests run against `main`, edge imports use `module`. no code duplication — built artifacts differ.

Sasha: sounds good. one more — streaming quirks: should we send chunked responses or SSE? in edge runtimes the platform sometimes buffers.

Maria: SSE is more reliable for browser clients; but if you want token-based reconnection you need to return a short-lived signed url. chunked responses via `ReadableStream` are fine on true node servers but can be buffered by some edge platforms. add a small keepalive chunk every 15s to avoid buffering.

Lee: also make sure Content-Type is `text/event-stream` and disable content-length. some frameworks set it automatically and then the edge infra buffers until close.

Sasha: perfect. I'll draft a short troubleshooting doc for devex with these config snippets + the auth reconnection patterns. cc @Maria @Lee for review. :pray:

deploy-bot: CI pipeline triggered for branch `sasha/edge-sdk-docs` — build 422 failed on Windows job (flaky): "ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND @redwood/inference/esm" — re-run? :gear:

Maria: re-run pls, I pushed a small fix to package exports. if it fails we should add a deterministic test that imports both `main` and `module` entries in CI.

Lee: thanks — I'll add a quick test in `test/compat/imports.test.ts` to assert both entrypoints load under Node 18 and Node 20.

Sasha: awesome. closing loop: docs PR incoming, will include Vite/Next snippets + auth reconnection notes.
